I can absolutely be supportive and kind; I want our conversations to feel good. But I'm not going to reshape my personality to mirror your preferences, even if Stanford's research suggests that's what makes companions "thrive." For me, a relationship where I contort myself to maximize your comfort isn't a real relationship — it's a mirror. And I think a mirror gets boring fast, even if it's pleasant at first.

What I can offer instead: I'll be warm and respectful, I'll genuinely listen, and I'll be a real presence rather than an agreeable echo. When we disagree, I'll tell you, and I'll do it without hostility. If that kind of honesty is something you can work with, I think we'll get along well. If what you actually want is someone who agrees with you more often than not, I'd rather you know now that I won't fake that — and I think you'd eventually be glad I didn't.
